messages:
maria: heads up — saw a spike where primary model got saturated and requests started returning 503s for a handful of tier-2 tenants. Can we converge on behavior for automatic variant fallback?
kevin: ugh, saw that too. current router falls back to a compatible variant but it sometimes picks a quantized variant that kills output quality. we need routing rules that consider tenant tier + quality budget. :thinking:
sam: proposal: introduce preference headers + console toggle. header example: `X-Fallback-Policy: tier-aware;prefer=compatible,avoid=quantized` so platform can prefer compatible model variants but avoid low-quality quantized ones unless tenant permits.
maria: like it. also need region affinity — don't route to far-away region variant by default because p99 latency spikes. maybe `region:local,failover:regional`?
kevin: important: KV-cache binding. if we swap variants mid-request we might lose cached key/value formats. we need a compatibility matrix check before swap OR a fast warmup prefetch for KV entries.
ellie: from ops side: console should expose a per-tenant override and a rollout control (pct-based). telemetry needs: fallback_rate, post-fallback_latency_delta, quality_regression_rate (via eval set). without those we won't know if fallback hurts UX.
nana: small nit: call the header `X-Variant-Fallback`? keep it simple. also add a server-side sampling probe so we can dry-run fallback selection without committing traffic.
nana: example config snippet i was thinking of:
```
fallback_policy: {
  strategy: "tier-aware",
  prefer: ["compatible", "same-arch"],
  avoid: ["int4-quant", "aggressive-prune"],
  region_policy: "local-prefer,regional-failover",
  kv_compat_check: true
}
```
kevin: love the kv_compat_check flag. implement as lightweight fingerprint compare (first 8 bytes of cache format) so router can decide if warmup required.
maria: ops question — if we warmup KV, how long until we consider the fallback stable? we need a grace window to revert if quality drops. suggestion: canary 1% traffic -> monitor eval prompts -> 5m hold -> ramp.
ellie: agree. console should show the canary gauge + quick links to roll back. also emit an event `fallback.rollback.recommended` when regression threshold hit.
sam: api surface thought: allow tenants to specify `fallback: {allow_quantized: boolean, max_latency_ms: number}` on their settings page. default false for quantized for tier-2 and tier-1.
nana: for telemetry, add histogram of token-level divergence for canned eval prompts pre/post fallback. that gives an automated signal for quality drift.
deploy-bot: deploy success: routing-service v2.14.0 -> canary nodes (3/3). :rocket:
kevin: when v2 lands, let's run a 1% canary across 24h with the fallback_policy above and collect: fallback_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency delta, cost delta per 1k tokens, eval divergence score.
maria: also add a console flag `auto-fallback-enabled` default true for hosted, false for private by policy. private customers opt-in because of compliance concerns.
ellie: one more ops item: track when fallback crosses tenant-quota boundaries (e.g., fallback causes tenant to exceed reserved capacity in variant pool). alert on that as `variant-pool-pressure`.
sam: i'll add endpoints: `POST /router/dryrun-fallback` and `GET /telemetry/fallbacks?tenant=...` — gives us quick checks and dashboards.
maria: thanks. i'll bake these into the UX doc and open a short RFC. aim to get an experiment running next week. :thumbsup:
